summary: verdaccio-okta-oauth preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-dictionary lookups) and, at install time, downloads the Bun runtime zip from a GitHub releases URL, unzips it to a temporary directory, chmod +x's the bun binary, and invokes it against a bundled ~727KB sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (single-line @bun-cjs bundle, shuffled string-array rotator, hex-named identifiers, fragmented URL-shaped constants) and is never reached through Node's normal require graph — it is executed only under the freshly dropped Bun binary. The package advertises itself as a Verdaccio Okta OAuth plugin and lists repository https://github.com/servicetitan/uikit.git, directory packages/verdaccio-okta-oauth, but nothing in the shipped code implements an OAuth flow; the alternate-runtime bootstrap and obfuscated payload are unrelated to the stated purpose and consistent with impersonation of an internal ServiceTitan package. Installing the package auto-executes attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine via a second language runtime, bypassing Node-based supply-chain scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
